title: Dynamic Routing for Micro-Retail Logistics
business: A regional logistics firm managing a fleet of micro-service containers that frequently scale based on warehouse activity.
problem: Manual updates to load balancer configurations during rapid container scaling lead to routing dead-ends and significant operational overhead.
solution: Traefik acts as a dynamic edge router that continuously queries the container orchestrator provider to discover new service endpoints in real-time, eliminating manual configuration updates.
steps: Deploy Traefik as the primary ingress controller within the container cluster.
Configure Traefik to connect to the orchestrator API as a service provider.
Define Entrypoints for incoming traffic on standard HTTP/HTTPS ports.
Apply labels to container services to instruct Traefik on routing rules and host matching.
Verify automatic route updates via the Traefik dashboard as containers spin up or down.
outcome: The infrastructure achieves seamless traffic distribution without human intervention or service restarts during scaling events.
limitation: Traefik relies on the consistency of the provider API; if the orchestrator API latency spikes, route discovery may lag, which can be monitored by checking the Traefik logs for provider synchronization errors.
